{{Quote|That's it, this is impossible! How do you communicate with these things?''"<br />"''That's it, this is impossible! How do you communicate with these things?''"<br />"''Shut up!''"<br />"''Shut up!|A student attempts to communicate with a Rishii|<ref name="EGTAS" />}}
The '''Rishii''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Bird/Legends|avian]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Rishi/Legends|Rishi]], possessing a generally [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] body structure, albeit with arms that functioned more like wings, a full-body covering of [[feather]]s, and eagle-like [[talons]] for feet. Rishii wings were uniquely "finger"-tipped, as well, an adaptation which, unlike most avian species, allowed them to both fly and manipulate objects. However, the species remained largely primitive in terms of engineering or technological advancement. A carnivorous species, the Rishii were well-regarded as friendly and accepting of others. They lived in small communes or groups known as nests, which existed harmoniously as well as with their off-worlder and non-Rishii neighbors, including followers of the [[H'kig]] religion who had settled on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].

Despite their apparent lack of advancement, Rishii were extremely intellectual, known for being polyglots and highly capable when it came to learning new languages, thanks to their innate mimicry abilities. This trait, occasionally, would cause confusion or misunderstandings between Rishii and off-worlders upon their first meeting, as the Rishii would instinctively repeat whatever was said to them. The [[Diet/Legends|predatory]] [[Maungur]] species, also native to Rishi, held a position of extreme importance in Rishii folklore; killing them was banned, despite the fact that the Maungur attacked and consumed the Rishii if the two ever crossed paths. 

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] [[Battle of Rishi (Clone Wars)|invaded]] Rishii in an attempt to capture [[Exonium/Legends|exonium]] mines used by the Rishii, who utilized the mineral to heat their [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] during [[Winter/Legends|winter]]. After [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] reinforcements arrived, the Rishii fought alongside [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] and [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] to defeat the Separatists and reclaim the mines.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Why you want to live in hot, humid lowlands? Mountains are much better.|A Rishii questions non-Rishii settlers' choice of home location|<ref name="DFRSB" />}}
The Rishii were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Bird/Legends|avian]] [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="DFR" /> of [[Diet/Legends|carnivores]]<ref name="EGTAS" /> which possessed a [[Color/Legends|brown]] and white-feathered<ref name="GOD" /> [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] form, with two [[Limb/Legends|legs]] ending in four-clawed, talon-like feet, two arms, a tail, and a head. The species' two arms consisted of feathered wings ending in<ref name="DFRSB" /> nimble<ref name="EGTAS" /> three-fingered humanoid hands, capable of manipulating tools. The wings allowed the Rishii to fly<ref name="DFRSB" /> at great speeds,<ref name="EGTAS" /> which was their method of travel equivalent to running in land-based species. A Rishii's head contained a beak between two yellow [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] framed by a large brow. Rishii were capable of mimicking anything said to them perfectly, and also possessed extremely strong senses, particularly hearing and sight. Rishii on average stood 1.6 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall<ref name="DFRSB" /> and had yellow skin.<ref name="GOD" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:Rishii_EGTA.png|thumb|left|230px|Rishii had forearms with both feathered wings and hands, which allowed them to fly and manipulate tools.]]
{{Quote|Energy from stones within mountain is needed for my kind to prepare food in the frost time.|Chieftain Gwarrk speaks about the Rishii's use of exonium|<ref name="GOD" />}}
Native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Rishi/Legends|Rishi]], the Rishii lived in loose primitive tribes,<ref name="DFR" /> known as nests,<ref name="DFRSB" /> clustered high upon the planet's [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]], away from the hot and humid lowland<ref name="DFR" /> [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]]. Each nest consisted of a small number of family units<ref name="DFRSB" /> led by a [[Chief/Legends|chieftain]],<ref name="GOD" /> with neighbouring nests respecting each other's territories and living in harmony. This peaceful and accepting attitude went beyond just other Rishii and was extended to all neighbours of a nest, including the many other species who eventually arrived from off-world to colonize the lowlands of Rishi. Due to the unfavorable conditions found in the lowlands, the native avians did not understand the off-worlders' choice to live there but were not opposed to their presence.<ref name="DFRSB" />

Despite their [[Human/Legends|Human]]-like hands allowing tools use, the Rishii only reached the point of using<ref name="DFRSB" /> bone,<ref name="EGTAS" /> stone and wood, being less technologically advanced even than the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] species of the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]. Some nests, however, did begin to trade with their non-Rishii neighbours in the lowlands, paying particular attention to the [[Starship/Legends|starships]] the off-worlders used to fly, which the avians believed were shiny rocks. These trading Rishii had no interest in using the technology they gained however, and used the various pieces they acquired to line the open-air nests and perches they dwelt in, which could be either natural or artificial. All Rishii naturally excelled at learning new languages, as they were able to perfectly mimic sounds they heard, and did so when hearing new words as a way of learning them. This repetition was often misinterpreted by non-Rishii as mockery, which could lead to trouble when individuals encountered Rishii for the first time.<ref name="DFRSB" />

The [[Diet/Legends|predatory]] [[Maungur]] creatures which inhabited the polar regions of Rishi held a position of extreme importance in Rishii belief and folklore. The creatures' name was the Rishii word for a "spirit of violent, senseless conflict that cannot be reasoned with", and the beasts were often used as characters in Rishii legend, being personified as conflict incarnate, a force of evil that had to be respected, acknowledged and feared. Not seen as evil, the Maungur appeared to be practically worshipped by the Rishii from an outsider's perspective, and [[Death/Legends|killing]] them was strictly forbidden, despite the fact that the animals preyed upon Rishii, along with anything else they encountered. The Rishii maintained that Maungur mainly ate [[khi'r]]s, a herbivorous species also native to Rishi, and as Maungur were rare and only dwelt in some of the low valleys, this was true for most of the [[Standard year/Legends|year]], but in the warmest season the Maungur would sometimes venture higher up the mountains and cause the Rishii to flee their homes to avoid conflict with the "spirit of Rishii". The Rishii avoided the valleys where Maungur could be found at all costs, and even avoided speaking about the predators if possible, as though the beasts could hear them.<ref name="CP">{{JournalCite|4|Creatures Preview}}</ref>

The Rishii's weapon of choice was the [[Sling/Legends|sling]], and each Rishii would build their own personal weapon to use.<ref name="DFRSB" /> This was because the avians were able to use the projectile weapons for hunting while in flight or on the ground. Rishii would also hunt by diving from great heights and grabbing their prey in their talons. Some Rishii also carried staffs.<ref name="EGTAS" /> In battle some Rishii also used [[Spear/Legends|spears]] or [[Axe/Legends|axes]] instead of slings. Rishii also made use of the mineral [[Exonium/Legends|exonium]], which they [[Mining/Legends|mined]] from the mountains they lived in. The stones were used by the avians to prepare food during [[Winter/Legends|winter]], which the Rishii knew as the "frost time".<ref name="GOD" />

==History==
[[File:Jungle_of_Rishi.jpg|thumb|left|Rishi, homeworld of the Rishii]]
At some point in the Rishiis' history, Humans and other off-world species belonging to the [[H'kig]] religion arrived on Rishi and began building settlements and [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] in the lowlands, the only areas suitable for them to live. The Rishii made contact with these [[Alien/Legends|aliens]], and after initial misunderstandings about the Rishii method of learning new languages, the two groups quickly came to peacefully co-exist, with some Rishii nests even starting to trade with the newcomers. Some attempts were made by the H'kig practitioners to convert the natives, but all met with failure and the return of the Rishii to their mountain-top homes.

When questioned by off-worlders on the Maungur, the natives were cryptic and unhelpful, with all non-Rishii understanding of the predators being pieced together from a large number of minor references and idle speculation, as no non-Rishii had ever definitely encountered a Maungur, although some possible run-ins were reported. When questioned as to the reason the Maungar had not reached the H'kig settlements also located in the lowlands the Rishii had few answered, only stating that the beasts had not found those areas yet. This led some non-Rishii to question the existence of Maungurs altogether, while those scientists who believed the natives theorized some form of pathogen may have prevented the maungur entering the inhabited valleys. As the Rishii showed no opposition to the settlement of the lowlands, off-worlders assumed Maungur territory was not sacred, or that the Rishii believed the settlers should learn of the dangers the predators posed the hard way.<ref name="CP" />

In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] a study conducted by the [[Rhinnal State Medical Academy]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] was published which listed Rishii as one of ten species most at risk due to air pollution. The test was carried out in middle class areas and concluded that pollution from government industrial centers and traffic was causing the problem, causing Rishii to develop diseases such as [[silicalung]] and [[lungrot]].<ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|49|life/13328_4.html|Study: Pollution Standards Still Endanger Many}}</ref>

[[File:Rishi_mines_attack.jpg|thumb|right|The Rishii fought alongside the Republic against the Separatists during the Clone Wars|220px]]
The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] sent forces to [[Battle of Rishi (Clone Wars)|invade]] Rishi during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], as exonium could be used to power their [[Sonic weapon/Legends|sonic weapons]] and so they hoped to seize the Rishiis' mines. In order to aid the primitive Rishii, the Republic and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] sent [[Green Company/Legends|Green Company]], a group of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], to help the natives in retaking the mines; however, when the troopers first arrived no [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] was available to command them and so they were ordered to wait until one arrived. [[Gwarrk]], a Rishii chieftain, took command of the troops in the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedis]]' absence, and ignoring the command to wait, sent the [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] in to attack the [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] warriors holding the mines.<ref name="GOD" />

Due to the tactical advantage the Geonosians' position gave the Separatists, the troopers were unable to defeat them and the attack was eventually called off when [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] arrived. Fisto then led an attack on the Separatist position alone, being covered by a [[Clone sharpshooter/Legends|clone sniper]] designated [[Cooker|2242]]. Once the Geonosians in the valley leading up to the mine were despatched, the remaining Republic and Rishii forces moved in to back up the Jedi, and the mine was quickly reclaimed, leading Gwarrk to greatly respect Fisto.<ref name="GOD" />

==Rishii in the galaxy==
In his travels of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] the [[Shi'ido]] [[sentientologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] encountered members of the Rishii species and memorized their form, later shapeshifting into a Rishii to escape from a number of [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]-employed [[Gank/Legends|Ganks]].<ref name="EGTAS" /> A Rishii known as [[Nazish]] became a member of the group known as the [[Zulirian Swordmasters]], and mastered the combat style of [[Trispzest]], which was developed by the [[S'kytri]] [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Kharys]]. The form focused on the use of flight against an opponent, and following Kharys [[Death/Legends|death]]<ref name="DFS">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050526a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 4: Of the Crudest Matter}}</ref> in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]<ref name="The Long Hunt">[[Star Wars Annual (1977) 1|''Star Wars Annual'' (1977) 1]]</ref> Nazish was left as one of only two beings who knew the style, the other being the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Maw (Dark Jedi)|Maw]].<ref name="DFS" />

==Behind the scenes==
Rishii were first mentioned in ''[[Dark Force Rising]]'', a [[Book/Legends|book]] written by [[Timothy Zahn]] and published in [[1992]]. The species were then depicted for the first time and given a more detailed description in the ''[[Dark Force Rising Sourcebook]]'' written by [[Bill Slavicsek]] for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' in [[1993]]. The first Rishii character to be named in a source was Nazish in [[2005]] in the fourth entry in the ''[[The Dark Forces Saga]]'', a supplement written for [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' by [[Abel G. Peña]] and [[Jason Fry]]. The first appearance of the species was not until [[Free Comic Book Day]] in [[2009]] when the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] [[The Gauntlet of Death|''The Clone Wars: The Gauntlet of Death'']] was released, with illustration by [[Ramón Pérez]] and writing by [[Henry Gilroy]].

In their first appearance the species name was spelled as "Rishi", the same as the name of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], but in all subsequent sources it was spelled "Rishii" apart from the [[1998]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] which also used the Rishi spelling.
